title.narrative: MSI hotline support for SEA reporting

description.narrative: ltpgtBackgroundltbrgtAllegations of sexual exploitation and abuse in Ethiopia are grossly underreported (for example, for the UN system, only 15 allegations have been received in 2024).nbsp This may be due to a number of factors, including stigma surrounding sexual abuse, barriers to reporting, fear of retaliation as well as lack of awareness regarding where to report.nbsp These factors are compounded by multiple reporting channels for each organization and at times, for each project.nbsp This creates confusion among communities as well as a gap in the reporting chain where the reporting channel is no longer functioning.nbsp ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtRationaleltbrgtThe PSEA Network, in conjunction with the AAP Working Group, conducted a mapping of SEA-related hotlines across the country.nbsp As a result of the mapping, it was clear that the MSI hotline for sexual and reproductive health was receiving the highest number of calls per month (over 10,000 calls) and operates in 5 languages (Amharic, English, Afan Oromo, Tigrigna, and one other language).nbsp There are plans to add Afar language.nbsp ltbrgtAs such, it is proposed that the existing MSI hotline is used as a complementary interagency hotline to receive allegations of SEA, and that this can be promoted by all actors operating in Ethiopialtbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtAdditional responsibilities – identifying, receiving and referring allegationsltbrgtThe additional responsibilities for MSI hotline operators include identifying, receiving and referral SEA allegations.nbsp These are explained below.nbsp ltbrgti) Identifying SEA allegationsltbrgtExisting hotline operators will be trained to identify SEA allegations among calls received.nbsp This will entail asking additional questions regarding the profile of the perpetrator, including which organization (if any) they belong to.nbsp Training and questions to be asked will be agreed upon between MSI and the PSEA Network.nbsp ltbrgtii) Receiving SEA allegationsltbrgtExisting hotline operators will be trained to receive SEA allegations from both community members and staff.nbsp Promotion of the MSI hotline will be included in community awareness-raising activities, which may be promoted via posters, banners, radio, video etc.nbsp ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtiii) Referring allegationsltbrgtOnce an SEA allegation has been identified, hotline staff are responsible for referring the allegation to the relevant organization where the alleged perpetrator works, if the victim/survivor consents.nbsp Where the survivor does not consent, or where the organization or perpetrator are not identified, the Ethiopia PSEA Network SEA referral procedures will be followed.nbsp Regular training will be provided by the PSEA Network on the referral procedures.nbsp ltbrgtNote on victim/survivor supportltbrgtAs the MSI hotline operators provide psychological first aid as well as counselling, these services will continue to be rendered to SEA victims/survivors.nbsp Referrals to other GBV services will also be made as per usual procedures, however for SEA allegations, support should also be provided by the alleged perpetrator’s organization as part of the Victim Assistance Protocol.nbsp This obligation is triggered as soon as an allegation of SEA is received (and not after investigation is concluded).nbsp ltbrgtHotline operator SOPsltbrgtThe PSEA Network Coordinator, in collaboration with the hotline manager, will draft SOPs for hotline operators together with an accompanying flow chart.nbsp ltbrgtPilot periodltbrgtThe proposed pilot period will be six months from the signing of any agreement with MSI to expand its hotline services.nbsp ltbrgtlt/pgt
